findings.description: Ranked fix 1 adds a rule to the session prompt's Searching section, which only routes questions to `Explore` subagents (2 of 111); the short-lived waste in cause 1 comes from `general-purpose` subagents (108 of 111), and the ready-to-add task wrongly calls the change a template edit with no code change.
findings.body:
**The ready-to-add fix 1 points at the wrong cause and misstates what it changes.**

Cause 1 measures `general-purpose` subagents: line 17 says 108 of 111 subagents are `general-purpose` and 2 are `Explore`. Line 34 then blames the Searching section of the session prompt. That section is `SESSION_SEARCHING` in `src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts:354-361`, and it only tells sessions to launch `subagent_type: "Explore"`. Nothing in the session prompt tells sessions to launch `general-purpose` subagents. The only such use is `SECURITY_REVIEW_AGENT = 'general-purpose'` for the conductor's security review. So the spike never shows where the 21 short-lived `general-purpose` launches come from. The link from the Searching section to cause 1 is unsupported.

The `pup plan add` text on line 64 also says "Only the prompt template changes, with no code change", and line 35 says "One line in the prompt template". There is no template. The text is a TypeScript constant in `src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts`. `test/unit/core/profile-compiler.test.ts` and `profile-compiler-context.test.ts` assert on the Searching text, so the task is a code and test change.

The acceptance criterion asks for a fix that can go straight to `pup plan add`. As written, an implementer would scope and cost the task wrongly. They would also have no evidence that the rule reaches the launches that cause the waste. A type-agnostic "no subagent for 1–2 call tasks" rule may still help, but the spike should say where `general-purpose` launches originate. It should also name the real file the rule goes in and drop the "no code change" claim.

findings.description: "Cause 3 below is the only lead" for the utility 49.3% is misleading: cause 3 is ruled out for subagents (line 46) and only its "Not checked" line mentions utilities, so say the utility cause is unexplained and a prefix change is an unchecked hypothesis.

process_issues.description: The validator confirmed the facts behind the important docs finding (SESSION_SEARCHING names only Explore, and there is no template file). It suggested downgrading the finding because the claim that the metric "would not move" is speculative. The orchestrator kept it as important but rewrote the body around the verified facts only.
